rationale: memory.undo re-applied only the fields of the previous history entry on the same step (memory.lua:401-412), found by step alone: a field the undone edit changed but that entry did not carry stayed changed (S42); apply_event's undo branch cleared the step's chord whenever that entry carried no chord degrees, and redo-all could not bring it back (S43); and the entry could be of another type or trig-lock parameter, so undoing a trig lock after another edit of the step left the lock in place (S44). Undo now restores the undone entry's saved original state for its key (song pattern, step, and for trig locks the parameter) and replays, in order, every earlier entry of the same type and key, so the step returns to its full state before the undone action. Redo, undo-all and redo-all are unchanged.
oracle: README 698-707 (Memory): memory retains all mask and trig lock actions; E3 scrolls left to explore past actions and right towards more recent ones; K3 jumps to the latest action. Human decision 2026-09-11 on S42-S44: undo restores the full prior step state.
